text:
rachel: heads-up: I built a tiny starter that wires Next.js app router + LangChain retriever against the Redwood API for a docs search demo. Hitting inconsistencies between client/edge/server SDK behavior on auth + retries.

tom: details? which runtime and which SDK version? :eyes:

rachel: using next@14 app router. Two entrypoints: an edge function for realtime search and server-side page rendering that pre-renders top results. Both call the same Redwood endpoint. SDKs: @redwood/js 0.13.0-edge for edge route, @redwood/js 0.13.0-node for server route (we split builds).

jess: Are you using same env var name in both contexts? edge needs NEXT_PUBLIC_ vs server-only REDWOOD_SERVER_KEY etc.

rachel: yes — edge uses NEXT_PUBLIC_REDFW_API (I know bad name, temporary) and server uses REDWOOD_SERVER_KEY. Still seeing a pattern: edge requests always succeed, server SSR sometimes gets 403 Forbidden on first hit after deploy, then heals. Logs show a retry loop that mutates headers: 

```
[redwood-sdk] request -> 403 Forbidden
[redwood-sdk] retry attempt 1, modifying auth header
[redwood-sdk] request -> 200 OK
```

tom: oof. 403 on first attempt implies something generating a short-lived token or rotating header. But you said server uses long-lived key?

rachel: dev key in env, long-lived. Minimal repro attached in devex/starters/next-langchain-search (small repo).

jess: I remember a change where the retry middleware tried to refresh tokens for non-2xx to handle transient auth refreshes, but it accidentally ran for static API keys in server runtime due to a missing runtime check. That could mutate header casing or add a prefix. I'll check commit history.

rachel: Workarounds I tried: 1) force no-retry in request options -> removes the 403 but then transient network failures fail too. 2) use serverless API route wrapper that reads key per-request -> reduced frequency but didn't eliminate the first-403 on cold deploy.

tom: Could the HTTP client reuse socket with stale TLS session in some Node versions? We had weirdness with http.Agent pooling + connection reuse causing repeated credential negotiation in older Node. Which Node version?

rachel: Node 20.21.0. Not super old.

jess: Good repro. I can replicate locally with your repo. Confirmed: retry logic calls an async token refresh hook unconditionally on 4xx in node runtime. It then overwrites Authorization header with an empty string for the first attempt and then sets the correct header on retry. So server sees 403 then 200.

rachel: ack. For the starter template we should document recommended pattern: 1) use explicit no-refresh flag for static keys 2) prefer per-request header set in a server API route 3) pin SDK until fix rolled out.

tom: Also worth adding a tiny integration test in the starter that does a cold-start fetch (spawn a fresh node process) and asserts no 4xx for a simple query. That will catch regressions during SDK changes.

jess: Plan: I'll open a patch to gate token-refresh logic behind runtime check (edge vs node and presence of refresh hook), and add a simple unit test. If that lands, we'll cut a patch release 0.13.1.

infra-bot: CI triggered for branch fix/avoid-unconditional-refresh. Status: queued.

rachel: Thanks! I'll update the starter README with explicit env examples (REDWOOD_SERVER_KEY vs NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY) and a note about Edge vs Node SDK parity. Also adding a tiny test script as tom suggested.

jess: Thanks for the clear repro + repo link — super helpful. This will also help our LangChain/LlamaIndex samples stay consistent across runtimes.

rachel: leaving the repo link in the issue and the PR. Will ping when tests land. :rocket:
